literal_campaign_claim: Proposition 4.5 constructs asymptotically valid confidence intervals for the stopping time using only a single simulation run.
actual_paper_statement: For fixed q in Q^bd and m0 in (0,1), under Assumption 4.1, v_hat_alpha converges almost surely to sigma_bd^2 as alpha decreases to zero; for every gamma in (0,1), the same-path plug-in interval covers the deterministic 1/KL_inf(q,m0) with limiting probability 1-gamma.
falsification_contract: The literal claim is contradicted by the proposition's exact coverage event. If the displayed interval is instead treated as an interval for its own observed tau_alpha/log(1/alpha), coverage is identically one because that value is the interval center, not 1-gamma.

tested_instance.assumption_4_1: Satisfied: q has endpoint atoms and bounded support {0,1}; mean 0.6 differs from m0.

acceptance.largest_b_coverage: Both 0.95 and 0.50 lie in their respective 95% Wilson intervals.
acceptance.largest_b_vhat_ratio: Mean and median v_hat/sigma_bd^2 are each in [0.97,1.03].
acceptance.largest_b_centering: Absolute relative centering error is at most 0.003.
acceptance.trends: Median and 90th-percentile absolute v_hat errors improve, and both coverage errors improve, from the first to the last scale.
acceptance.controls: The finite-alpha large-scale gate and wrong KL_inf^2 denominator must fail; treating the interval as covering its own stopping time must yield tautological coverage one at both nominal levels.

verdict_scope: FALSIFIED as literally supplied: Proposition 4.5 does not claim nominal coverage for a random stopping time. The actual displayed proposition is also directly supported for a nondegenerate Bernoulli law; that finite experiment is not a proof over every q in Q^bd.
